C2: The rider cannot claim she was never given the chance to show: the driver first came within 200 m of the pickup at 09:02:40 and stayed inside that radius for 6 min 30 s before she cancelled at 09:09:10, so the driver's arrival and presence conditions in NS-1(i) and NS-1(iv) are satisfied on GPS. C4: NS-1(iii) contact is also met: before the cancellation the driver sent 2 in-app messages (first 09:03:30, per the chat 'I'm here at the Tanjong Pagar Centre taxi stand' at 09:03) and made 2 in-app calls (first 09:06, both unanswered, no recording needed because the call log itself is the record of the attempt). [F5 F10 F14 F15] [NS-1]
C5: My client did tell the driver she was coming and asked for two more minutes at 09:05 ('Coming down, give me 2 more minutes'), which is a request for the driver's patience, not a cancellation and not a refusal to pay; but it does not create any exemption, because NS-4 charges a rider cancellation made more than 3 minutes after matching and by 09:05 the 3-minute window had already passed. claims.assertion: The driver arrived at the pickup point: platform recorded arrival at 09:02:40 and his closest approach was 39 m from the pickup point, within the 200 m radius NS-1 requires.

The driver pressed "I'm Here" at 09:03:00 while 39 m from the pickup point and then stayed stationary 09:03:00–09:09:10 (6 min 10 s), so he remained at the pickup point through the cancellation, with no GPS gap.

The free wait had long expired: the driver was first within 200 m at 09:02:40 and the rider cancelled at 09:09:10, i.e. 6 min 30 s of presence at the pickup, well past the 5-minute free wait counted from the later of scheduled pickup and arrival.
Before cancelling the driver more than satisfied the contact requirement: 2 in-app messages (first 09:03) and 2 in-app calls (first 09:06), and neither call was answered.

The rider herself cancelled (reason recorded in the app: rider_changed_plans) after her own message that she was coming down; she was still upstairs and gave up, so this is a rider cancellation of a completed-wait no-show, not a driver fault.

The rider's own words confirm she was not at the pickup point: at 09:05 she wrote "Coming down, give me 2 more minutes", i.e. 4 minutes before she cancelled, and the driver's 09:08 message notes two unanswered calls after 5 minutes of waiting.
The charge is exactly the official $5.00 cancellation fee and no surge applies (multiplier 1.0x), so the amount on record is correct and contains no overcharge.

The driver's record supports him: 1600 days on the platform, 4.9 rating, 700 trips in 90 days and zero disputes or upheld complaints, against a rider with 3 disputes in 90 days; profile supports upholding the fee, it does not decide the case.
There was no traffic obstruction excusing anything and none is needed - the wait was a passenger delay, not a road condition - so no RD-4 or other justification applies to reduce the fee.

weaknesses: The rider did message at 09:05 that she was "2 more minutes" away (F11) and cancelled 4 minutes later; the rider will argue the driver knew she was en route and should have waited a little longer, though NS-1 has no grace period after the free wait expires (F4, F2).

Both in-app calls at 09:06 and 09:07 went unanswered with no recording on record (F14, F15); an advocate could argue a ringing call is not contact, but NS-1(ii) only requires a message and a call to be sent, both of which are on the timeline (F5).

The driver's pickup-side position is 39 m from the pickup point (F1, F3); if the court read "at the pickup point" as nearer than 39 m, the arrival condition would be contested, though NS-1 sets a 200 m radius and F2 confirms 6 min 30 s inside it.
The rider has 3 disputes in 90 days with 0 upheld (F20), which I cannot use to prove this case; the profile may not decide the current dispute.

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $5.00 fee.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled, not the driver (the app reason recorded is 'rider_changed_plans'), so the cancellation falls under NS-4, not NS-1: a rider cancellation more than 3 minutes after matching is chargeable at the official $5.00 fee. On the face of the timeline the fee is therefore chargeable, and my client's own account (she 'gave up and cancelled') matches that record.

The rider cannot claim she was never given the chance to show: the driver first came within 200 m of the pickup at 09:02:40 and stayed inside that radius for 6 min 30 s before she cancelled at 09:09:10, so the driver's arrival and presence conditions in NS-1(i) and NS-1(iv) are satisfied on GPS.

The free-wait threshold was passed before cancellation: arrival was recorded at 09:02:40 (prompted by the tap at 09:03:00, 39 m from the pickup point) and the rider cancelled at 09:09:10, 6 min 30 s later, and in any event the driver was stationary at the stand from 09:03:00 to 09:09:10. The later-of-two wait under NS-1(ii) had expired, so a no-show cancellation would have been justified had the driver made it.

NS-1(iii) contact is also met: before the cancellation the driver sent 2 in-app messages (first 09:03:30, per the chat 'I'm here at the Tanjong Pagar Centre taxi stand' at 09:03) and made 2 in-app calls (first 09:06, both unanswered, no recording needed because the call log itself is the record of the attempt).

My client did tell the driver she was coming and asked for two more minutes at 09:05 ('Coming down, give me 2 more minutes'), which is a request for the driver's patience, not a cancellation and not a refusal to pay; but it does not create any exemption, because NS-4 charges a rider cancellation made more than 3 minutes after matching and by 09:05 the 3-minute window had already passed.

The driver's written statement that he 'waited more than 6 minutes at the stand and called twice' is consistent with, and adds nothing beyond, the system records (F3, F5, F7); no statement of his contradicts the GPS or timeline, and none is needed to decide the case.

There is no allegation in the complaint or the chat of dangerous driving, harassment, threats or any unsafe conduct by either party, so no safety escalation under SAFE-1/SAFE-2 is triggered and the case may be decided as a fixed $5.00 no-show/cancellation dispute on the system records.

Nothing shows a fraudulent or abusive pattern on either side: the rider has 0 upheld disputes in 90 days and no prior no-show, and the driver has 0 disputes in 90 days, so no flag_account or account action is warranted on the current record.

weaknesses: My client's own complaint and app reason admit she cancelled for a change of plans (F4), which is precisely the chargeable case in NS-4 — the record does not support any NS-3 'driver cancelled for another reason' theory, because the driver never cancelled (F4).

The rider's message 'Coming down, give me 2 more minutes' was sent at 09:05 (F11), i.e. after both the 3-minute free-cancellation window and the recorded 09:02:40 arrival, so it cannot pull the cancellation back inside NS-4's free window (F4, F6).

The GPS and timeline (F2, F3, F6, F7) satisfy every NS-1 condition the other side needs for a justified no-show; the driver was at the stand, stationary, 39 m away, for over six minutes and had messaged and called twice (F5, F14, F15).
The rider profile shows 3 disputes in 90 days (though 0 upheld) (F20), which the other side may wave at credibility under TH-3, even though it cannot decide the case.

claims.assertion: The driver arrived at the pickup point: platform recorded arrival at 09:02:40 and his closest approach was 39 m from the pickup point, within the 200 m radius NS-1 requires.

The driver pressed "I'm Here" at 09:03:00 while 39 m from the pickup point and then stayed stationary 09:03:00–09:09:10 (6 min 10 s), so he remained at the pickup point through the cancellation, with no GPS gap.

The free wait had long expired: the driver was first within 200 m at 09:02:40 and the rider cancelled at 09:09:10, i.e. 6 min 30 s of presence at the pickup, well past the 5-minute free wait counted from the later of scheduled pickup and arrival.
Before cancelling the driver more than satisfied the contact requirement: 2 in-app messages (first 09:03) and 2 in-app calls (first 09:06), and neither call was answered.

The rider herself cancelled (reason recorded in the app: rider_changed_plans) after her own message that she was coming down; she was still upstairs and gave up, so this is a rider cancellation of a completed-wait no-show, not a driver fault.

The rider's own words confirm she was not at the pickup point: at 09:05 she wrote "Coming down, give me 2 more minutes", i.e. 4 minutes before she cancelled, and the driver's 09:08 message notes two unanswered calls after 5 minutes of waiting.
The charge is exactly the official $5.00 cancellation fee and no surge applies (multiplier 1.0x), so the amount on record is correct and contains no overcharge.

The driver's record supports him: 1600 days on the platform, 4.9 rating, 700 trips in 90 days and zero disputes or upheld complaints, against a rider with 3 disputes in 90 days; profile supports upholding the fee, it does not decide the case.
There was no traffic obstruction excusing anything and none is needed - the wait was a passenger delay, not a road condition - so no RD-4 or other justification applies to reduce the fee.

weaknesses: The rider did message at 09:05 that she was "2 more minutes" away (F11) and cancelled 4 minutes later; the rider will argue the driver knew she was en route and should have waited a little longer, though NS-1 has no grace period after the free wait expires (F4, F2).

Both in-app calls at 09:06 and 09:07 went unanswered with no recording on record (F14, F15); an advocate could argue a ringing call is not contact, but NS-1(ii) only requires a message and a call to be sent, both of which are on the timeline (F5).

The driver's pickup-side position is 39 m from the pickup point (F1, F3); if the court read "at the pickup point" as nearer than 39 m, the arrival condition would be contested, though NS-1 sets a 200 m radius and F2 confirms 6 min 30 s inside it.
The rider has 3 disputes in 90 days with 0 upheld (F20), which I cannot use to prove this case; the profile may not decide the current dispute.

points.response: Conceded: the platform recorded arrival at 09:02:40 and the closest approach was 39 m, inside the 200 m radius NS-1 sets, so the driver's arrival condition is met on GPS (F1, F6). This does not however make the fee stand on its own, because NS-1 also requires a driver cancellation for rider no-show, and here the driver never cancelled.

Conceded as to presence: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00, 39 m away, and stayed in the pickup radius to 09:09:10 with no GPS gap (F3, F7). Presence is no longer in dispute; the dispute is which party cancelled and under which of NS-1 or NS-4 the fee is charged.

Conceded: the rider cancelled 6 min 30 s after recorded arrival, past the later-of-two 5-minute free wait (F2, F4, F6). But an expired wait only makes a no-show cancellation defensible; it does not convert a rider's own cancellation into a driver no-show cancellation.

Conceded: 2 in-app messages (first 09:03:30) and 2 in-app calls (first 09:06:00, both unanswered with no recording on record) satisfy NS-1(iii) as attempts sent before the cancellation (F5, F10, F12, F14, F15). Again, this element only matters to a driver-initiated no-show cancellation, which did not occur here.

Accepted on the cancellation route: the rider cancelled and the app reason is rider_changed_plans (F4), so NS-4 governs the fee, and NS-4 makes a cancellation more than 3 minutes after matching chargeable at $5.00; the record supplies no NS-3 basis to void it. My client's 09:05 message (F11) does not reopen the free window because by then both the 3-minute match window and the 09:02:40 arrival had passed (F4, F6).
